title: Advanced Practices After Opening the Governing Vessel
author: Li Shaobo

inline.s: Most people who study the True Qi Circulation Method on their own, upon reaching the stage of "opening the Governing Vessel," believe they have completed all five steps of the practice. In fact they have completed only the first four steps of its elementary stage, and very few ever grasp the fifth step. Even when someone enters stillness well, the advanced states that arise in that stillness often vanish through fear and incomprehension, leaving their progress stalled. For this reason, I offer here a brief account of the states that naturally appear in the course of the fifth step, so as to point the way for those who wish to practice the True Qi Circulation Method in depth.

The meaning of "the primordial spirit stores power and nurtures vitality" is this: a deeply stilled state of "tranquil emptiness" — that is, the primordial spirit — allows the material substance and motive force of life (essence, qi, and spirit) to gather and combine, thereby nurturing a vigorous vital function.

The fifth step of the True Qi Method is practiced in a state of deep stillness. Accordingly, when practicing the fourth step, the student should hold a correct understanding of opening the Governing Vessel and of the sensation of qi: opening the Governing Vessel is only the mark of entering the gate. In qigong, the sensation of qi is merely a product of the elementary stage. As stillness deepens and power grows, the sensation of qi stabilizes and then turns into embryonic breathing and on into the void, entering the realm of light...

This means that during the stage of opening the Governing Vessel, you must never let the ever-shifting sensations of qi entangle you and give rise to scattered thoughts, and still less should you guide the qi with intention in pursuit of sensation once it has stabilized. Devote yourself wholly to "stillness," and the following four levels of practice will naturally appear: 1. Guide the qi along its course and circulate the microcosmic orbit; 2. Abide in stillness through embryonic breathing and dissolve into the void; 3. Break through the void and behold the light; 4. Seek the true body in the depths of the auspicious light.

blocks.text: 1. Guide the Qi Along Its Course and Circulate the Microcosmic Orbit

inline.s: Method: After the Governing Vessel opens, you may once again follow the first step ("
Breathe and focus attention on the pit of the stomach
") and hold your intention there. When, in the course of practice, the qi sensation at the pit of the stomach moves naturally down toward the lower dantian, you may follow the second step ("
Let intention and breath descend together toward the dantian
") and guide the true qi into the lower dantian, then follow the third step ("
Regulate the breath, gather the spirit, and guard the dantian
") and hold your intention at the lower dantian. When the true qi enters the Governing Vessel, practice the fourth step ("
When the Governing Vessel opens, neither forget nor force

"). When the true qi becomes active in the head, do not rush to guide it downward; wait in stillness, and the true qi will pass naturally through the yintang and run down along the nose. At this point you may, following its natural course, return to the first step once more.

In this way the first four steps, guided according to the natural movement of the true qi, alternate between movement and stillness and complete a circuit of the orbit within a single session. Usually several circuits can be completed naturally in one session.

Responses: As the true qi grows vigorous and the meridians are opened and regulated, local responses gradually stabilize and give way to whole-body sensations of warmth, coolness, largeness, smallness, lightness, and heaviness. "Warmth" means that when one enters stillness in practice the whole body feels as if bathed in spring sunshine — warm, comfortable, and joyful. "Coolness" means that in stillness one feels as if strolling beneath a bright moon, the mind open and serene. "Largeness" means that one feels the body to be towering and boundless; "
smallness
" means that one feels the body shrinking.

Timing: In the course of guiding the qi and circulating the orbit, as stillness deepens, at times the breath becomes extremely fine and slow. This is the sign that embryonic breathing is emerging; you may hold to this excellent state of stillness and abide in it silently. If a thought stirs even slightly, the primordial spirit at once turns into the acquired mind, and the fine state of stillness is broken. Embryonic breathing is a natural response that comes after the Governing Vessel opens and stillness deepens. The time at which it appears differs from person to person: the better one's stillness, the sooner embryonic breathing arrives.

blocks.text: 2. Abide in Stillness Through Embryonic Breathing and Dissolve Into the Void

inline.s: Method: When embryonic breathing arises naturally in practice, you may cease guarding the dantian and, following its natural course, remain in that fine state of stillness.

Responses: At first embryonic breathing lasts only briefly and occurs rarely; as stillness deepens it occurs more often and its duration naturally lengthens. As the time of embryonic breathing grows longer in each session, there appears the experience of the body dissolving into the void and ceasing to exist. At first only part of the body dissolves into the void; as power grows, the whole body seems to disappear, and one enters the state of "forgetting both self and object."
Timing: Once you enter the void of "forgetting both self and object," follow its natural course and settle your stillness upon the void.

blocks.text: 3. Break Through the Void and Behold the Light

inline.s: Method: When the void of "forgetting both self and object" appears in practice, settle your stillness naturally upon the void. Do not seek the dantian again, nor let any thought of pursuit arise and break the fine state of deep stillness.

Responses: As the state of void stabilizes, ordinary chronic ailments can be cured and one comes to possess the ability to emit inner qi outward — though it is best not to use it. Keep the mind wholly still and fixed, and aim directly at the highest attainment.

Timing: When a flash of bright light appears at the yintang during practice, it shows that one's power has reached the middle level. At first the bright light flashes and vanishes, unsteady. As stillness becomes mature, the elixir light naturally stabilizes, and one may then practice within the realm of light.

blocks.text: 4. Seek the True Body in the Depths of the Auspicious Light

inline.s: Method: When a steady bright light appears at the yintang in practice, you may fix your stillness upon the center of that light. Within the light a further light will stand out; continue to fix your stillness upon its center, and still another light will emerge — and so continue. Alternatively, when the bright light appears at the yintang, send it into the lower dantian and fix your stillness upon the center of the light there; or settle the light upon the position of the middle dantian.

Responses: Light is the middle-to-higher level of qigong practice. In the early stage of cultivating light, because the mind is not yet pure and still, the bright light is easily transformed — into mountains, streams, grass, and trees, or into human forms. All manner of illusory scenes, changing with one's thoughts, will disturb one's stillness. You must look upon them as if seeing nothing, keep the mind wholly still, and hold fast to the bright light; then the illusory scenes will vanish, and there will appear red, white, green, blue, yellow, and purple auspicious lights. Fix your stillness wholly upon the center of the auspicious light; when power reaches a certain level, your own form will appear within the light. Daoists call this "the Red Infant"; Buddhists call it "the Dharma body." In essence, it is a response of one's own life-information concentrated to a high degree.

Timing: The cultivation of light is the middle-to-higher level of qigong and belongs to the scope of xing gong (nature practice). The higher one's power, the more it depends on spiritual insight and on the cultivation of virtue: through cultivating virtue one deepens insight and penetrates the workings of practice.
